svg.title: How long can a first-party cookie last in Safari?
svg.desc: Bar chart of Safari's maximum lifetime for first-party cookies, in days. A cookie written by JavaScript: 7 days, deleted after 7 days without user interaction. A JavaScript cookie written on a landing page reached from a tracker-classified domain with a query string or fragment: 1 day. A server-set cookie from a subdomain that is CNAME- or IP-cloaked to a third party: 7 days. A server-set cookie from your own infrastructure: the expiry you set, which Chrome caps at 400 days for every cookie.
svg.text: How long can a first-party cookie last in Safari?
Maximum lifetime in days. How the cookie is written, and by whose server, decides the cap.

g.text: landing URL with a query string or fragment
subdomain CNAME- or IP-mapped to another party
same origin, or a same-party IP range

svg.text: The expiry you set (beyond this chart)
Chrome caps every cookie at 400 days. GA4's default _ga expiry is 2 years. Detection of third-party IP addresses is heuristic and may change.
Sources: WebKit tracking prevention policy, ITP 2.1 and 2.2, CNAME cloaking defense, Private Browsing 2.0; Chrome for Developers; GA4 cookie usage help.
